summary: Lite preserves the main opening counts on all three facades and generates simpler artwork quickly. It loses material and glazing detail, changes balcony barriers and misreads wires as window railings. It has not demonstrated equal quality to the previous built-in raster generator. None of these outputs is accepted as measured facade geometry.

retained: Three upper rows with one broad left and two narrow right windows
errors: Dark uniform panels replace observed glazed panes
Green lintels and bands are exaggerated and regularized
Material becomes smooth reddish-brown rather than visible brick
Tall output changes spacing and framing
findings.comparison: Previous built-in raster retains more frame and brick detail, though it also changes framing and colour.

retained: Three upper rows with two windows left and three right
errors: Varied/glazed balcony barriers replaced by repeated dark metal railings
Small glass-block opening at ground left omitted
Grey left door loses its porthole
findings.comparison: Previous built-in raster is closer on balcony glazing and left door detail; neither fully matches the ground floor.

retained: Left gable and top arched-left/rectangular-right pair
errors: Crossing photo wires appear as extra rails on side windows
Stone lintel and keystone shapes exaggerated
Blank lower area loses some observed shop evidence
Sign lettering partly copied despite prompt asking no guessed lettering
findings.comparison: Leaving occluded areas plain is preferable to invented shop openings, but the output also removes visible storefront evidence. Prior built-in raster invented a more complete shopfront.

limitations: Lite 1K and supported aspect ratios differ from prior automatic output dimensions
Source identity and world registration remain unresolved
Visual judgments are not measured accuracy
